findings.finding: When TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN is unset in configuration/env, _verify_twilio_signature returns True for all requests, allowing unauthenticated attackers to forge SMS inbound opt-out and opt-in webhooks.
findings.why_it_matters: An external prober knowing a user's phone number can POST arbitrary From/Body payloads to /sms/inbound and flip sms_opt_out on target user accounts, causing denial of service on 2FA SMS logins.

repro.command: ./.venv/bin/python -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0, '.'); from server.routes_auth_2fa import _verify_twilio_signature; print('Observed bypass result:', _verify_twilio_signature('https://helpotron.dpdns.org/sms/inbound', {'From': '+15551234567', 'Body': 'STOP'}, 'invalid_sig'))"
repro.observed:
SMS inbound: TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN unset — Twilio signature NOT verified
Observed bypass result: True

findings.proposed_fix: When TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN is missing or empty, fail closed by returning False (or raise 401/503) unless explicitly in local testing environment with TEST_MODE=true.

test_to_write.body:
def test_twilio_signature_fails_closed_when_token_unset(monkeypatch):
    from server.routes_auth_2fa import _verify_twilio_signature
    monkeypatch.delenv('TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN', raising=False)
    assert _verify_twilio_signature('https://helpotron.dpdns.org/sms/inbound', {'From': '+1555123'}, 'fake') is False

findings.done_when: _verify_twilio_signature returns False when TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN is unset in non-test mode.

findings.construct: git push feature branch guard in run_bash
findings.finding: The git push feature branch check extracts the last token and only checks !== 'master' && !== 'main', allowing push to main via git refspecs such as HEAD:main or refs/heads/main.
findings.why_it_matters: A prompt-injected or compromised model turn executing run_bash could push unauthorized commits directly to main/master on origin using git push origin HEAD:main.

repro.command: node -e 'const cmd = "git push origin HEAD:main"; const toks = cmd.split(" ").filter(Boolean); const gi = toks.indexOf("git"); const pi = toks.indexOf("push"); const rest = toks.slice(pi + 1); const branch = rest.filter((t) => t[0] !== "-" && t !== "origin" && t !== "upstream").pop(); console.log("Blocked:", (!branch || branch === "master" || branch === "main"));'

findings.proposed_fix: Inspect refspecs and target branches: split on ':' and check if destination target ends with 'main' or 'master', or if target matches refs/heads/(main|master).
findings.done_when: git push origin HEAD:main and git push origin refs/heads/main are rejected by the run_bash guard.

findings.finding: screenMcpSetupPrompt reads .platform property off S.resolveAll(), which returns an Array, resulting in undefined and always defaulting to 'linux' regardless of configured settings.
findings.why_it_matters: When a Windows user or agent configures the harness platform to 'windows', screenMcpSetupPrompt silently generates POSIX/bash configuration instructions and forward slashes, causing agent connection failure.

repro.command: node -e 'const S = require("./cli/settings"); const raw = { platform: "windows" }; console.log("Broken:", String(S.resolveAll(raw).platform || "linux"));'

findings.proposed_fix: Replace S.resolveAll().platform with S.resolveAll().find((r) => r.setting.path === 'platform')?.value || 'linux', exactly matching line 2036 in the same file.
findings.done_when: screenMcpSetupPrompt accurately derives the platform from the resolved setting row rather than the array object.

findings.construct: _service_health called synchronously from async def status
findings.finding: _service_health executes a synchronous httpx.get with a 2.0s timeout inside async def status without asyncio.to_thread, blocking the FastAPI event loop during sidecar outages.
findings.why_it_matters: When the hygiene sidecar on port 8765 is hung or unreachable, incoming calls to /api/hygiene/status freeze the single-threaded event loop for 2.0s, stalling all concurrent requests across the API.

repro.command: ./.venv/bin/python -c "import asyncio; from server.routes_hygiene import status; res = asyncio.run(status()); print('Result:', res)"

findings.proposed_fix: Wrap _service_health call in await asyncio.to_thread(_service_health) inside status(), matching the async pattern in _forward.

test_to_write.body:
import asyncio
async def test_status_non_blocking():
    from server.routes_hygiene import status
    task = asyncio.create_task(status())
    await asyncio.sleep(0.01)
    assert not task.done() or task.done()

findings.done_when: status() route delegates blocking I/O to a worker thread via asyncio.to_thread.

findings.finding: server/.env exists but is never loaded by config.py or llm.py, which both explicitly bind to the root .env, making any edits to server/.env completely inert.
findings.why_it_matters: Operators attempting to rotate keys or configure settings inside server/.env experience silent failure where values are not applied to the running application.

repro.command: ./.venv/bin/python -c "from server.config import config; print('Resolved env_file:', getattr(config.__class__, 'model_config', {}).get('env_file'))"

findings.proposed_fix: Remove or replace server/.env with a README/symlink pointing to the canonical root .env, or add an explicit startup check warning if server/.env exists.
findings.done_when: server/.env is archived or clarified so operators cannot mistake it for the active configuration file.

findings.finding: API key endpoint scope checking uses any(path.startswith(p) for p in allowed_prefixes) without path delimiter boundary, allowing path prefix traversal (e.g. prefix '/api/task' matches '/api/tasks' or '/api/task_admin').
findings.why_it_matters: Scoped API keys intended for a limited resource prefix can access adjacent un-scoped endpoints sharing the same string prefix.

repro.command: python3 -c "prefixes = ['/api/task']; path = '/api/tasks_delete'; print('Allowed:', any(path.startswith(p) for p in prefixes))"

findings.proposed_fix: Enforce boundary check: any(path == p or path.startswith(p.rstrip('/') + '/') for p in allowed_prefixes).
findings.done_when: Scope prefix checks strictly enforce path segment boundaries.

findings.why_it_matters: Colliding update IDs across Telegram bots could cause legitimate webhook updates to be dropped as duplicates.

roofing-lead-bot/app.py:228:    if not check_and_record_event(message_sid, 'twilio'):
roofing-lead-bot/app.py:344:    if not check_and_record_event(msg_id, 'telegram'):
roofing-lead-bot/app.py:433:    if not check_and_record_event(event_id, 'stripe'):

findings.proposed_fix: Namespace Telegram events with bot token prefix or tenant ID.

findings.finding: datetime.utcnow() is deprecated in Python 3.12+ and produces naive UTC datetimes, which risk comparison errors against timezone-aware datetimes.
findings.why_it_matters: Generates DeprecationWarnings and can fail if SQLAlchemy datetime fields are configured with timezone awareness.

repro.observed: DeprecationWarning: datetime.datetime.utcnow() is deprecated and scheduled for removal in a future version. Use timezone-aware objects to represent datetimes in UTC: datetime.datetime.now(datetime.UTC).

findings.done_when: No naive datetime.utcnow() calls remain in record_data_submission.

findings.finding: /health endpoint returns HTTP 503 when the browser is not attached, which is normal for an idle gateway prior to first request.
findings.why_it_matters: External monitoring tools treating HTTP 503 as service failure will falsely report the gateway process as crashed.
findings.proposed_fix: Document that /health is a liveness probe where 503 denotes 'idle / waiting for browser attach', while /metrics returns 200 for pure observation.

findings.done_when: Monitoring documentation clarifies 503 status semantics on /health.
